I think the RX 5700 is still in a good spot. If we compare the RX 5700 specs vs the RTX 2060 Super we will see they are very similar in SP/CUDA Cores, and even power consumption with the RX 5700 consuming about 5 more watts than the 2060 Super. The 5700 also has higher clock speeds which will probably make it a bit faster than the 2060 Super. Add Radeon Anti-Lag (FFX isn't that much needed) and the 5700 could still be a viable option.


Over at the 5700 XT we see much of the same story. Considering the 5700 XT's performance advantage shown through AMD slides with it beating the vanilla RTX 2070 by quite a decent margin, it seems that it could be on par with the RTX 2070 Super. The 5700 XT only consumes about 10 more watts compared to the 2070 Super, has the same amount of Stream Processors to that of NVIDIA's CUDA cores, and has higher clock speeds than 2070 Super. It also has the same Radeon Anti-Lag and FFX that you get with the RX 5700 as well as other GCN cards.


Comparing the 5700 XT to the Vega 56, according to AMD, in games it performs 25-40% faster at roughly the same power for $100 launch price ($200 for today's prices) is good.
